title: New to ai trading - Is my strategy 💩 ?
author: Acm13
selftext:
I'm fairly new to using the Robinhood MCP, and I'm not a seasoned investor. I would appreciate any guidance or insight on a few things. 

1. Is there a way to have the model make trades without having to confirm each time?   
Basically having the model to react in real time if I'm not keeping an eye on things. 

2. What do you find is the best use of ai for trading?  
My strategy so far has been to have the model use the Robinhood screener to find undervalued companies and then suggest a limit buy and limit sell for an exit if things go south. 

3. Do you think ai trading is better suited for trading options, and also is there a minimum account blanced need to unlock options on the agentic account? b.c i don't have it

I only started with about $700 as a test using AI, and my goal is to grow it to $1000 in a few months, and then invest more once I have a proven strategy 

https://preview.redd.it/lbiwmyyyr3fh1.png?width=1053&format=png&auto=webp&s=21f05165eafad7ecd07e661fa7fbc05bf5fe2850

comments.author: jaw_line
comments.body:
Using ai to find stocks is basically everyone’s first thought/application. It works for some, for me I don’t like that ai’s can discern, getting two results from one piece of data is something you should avoid as a general rule of thumb in trading anything.

There’s a lot to learn and this is a very very new space

replies.author: Acm13
replies.body:
Interesting thanks for the insight.

So do you come up with ideas and then run them though ai to refine? Or are u going full automation

replies.author: jaw_line
replies.body: You can and should do both. You are already thinking in the right direction, go to library get some trading books and get to back testing

comments.author: s_lw0
comments.body:
i would not let it trade without confirmation yet

ai is useful for research screening summarizing filings and checking ideas
but full auto execution is where it gets dangerous fast

with 700 dollars i would focus on paper trading the workflow first
and if you use api access make sure withdrawals are disabled

also options is probably not the best place to test this
too many ways to lose fast before you know if the system even works

replies.author: Powerful-Field-4730
replies.body: Ya I heard options not the way to go with algo trading for 1 they are too expensive

replies.author: Acm13
replies.body: Thanks for the insight. I dont think u can even turn off confirmation with robinhood right now so i should be safe.

comments.author: CryptographerBig7624
comments.body:
fair questions, one thing on #1 though, i'd be careful wishing for fully autonomous execution this early. the value of AI here isn't reacting in real time for you, it's helping you build and test a rule set you actually understand. a model left to trade unsupervised on $700 will find creative ways to lose it, not because it's dumb but because it has no real edge, it's just pattern-matching plausible-looking trades.

honestly the most useful thing i've found is using it to analyze what went wrong after the fact and to invalidate weak ideas fast, not to make live calls. let it propose, you dispose. the moment it's pulling the trigger unsupervised you've automated a strategy you haven't proven yet, which is the expensive way to learn.

can't help on the robinhood options side, different setup than what i run

comments.author: hikewithcaramel
comments.body: I run an LLM bot alongside three others purely as an experiment. It only trades Gold and Brent. I have Gold and Brent in other bots so I can correlate whether an LLM proposing is better than a deterministic rules based bot. All the other bots have hard coded strategy, entry and exit parameters. Sandboxes in month 2 at the moment but the LLM creates logs based on its decisions to turn down a trade and we'll as enter one. It has control over what to trade, which direction and how to close but it still has to meet a coded guardrail regime for the trigger to be pulled
